page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.10xlarge is a compute-focused instance from the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor on x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor featuring 20 physical cores, 40 dedicated vCPUs, and 35 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, BMI2, and FMA. It is provisioned with 96.0 GB of memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU allocation of 2.4 GB per thread.

Hardware capabilities do not include local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent data. The network subsystem delivers a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the instance performs consistently within the middle 50% across compute, memory, and application-level metrics. It achieved a multi-core stress-ng score of 38,381.56 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,735.0, alongside 161.64 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 34.66 million operations per second in Redis SET tests.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high compute density and clock rates relative to its hardware class without the overhead of bundled local storage or attached GPUs. The 2.4 GB per core ratio keeps resource balancing centered on compute-heavy tasks rather than vast in-memory footprints. This profile aligns well with software compilation, high-concurrency web serving, batch compression, CI/CD runners, and distributed compute workloads requiring high single-core frequency.

The instance contains 96.0 GB of system memory (2.4 GB per vCPU) and a baseline network throughput of 12 Gbps. Standardized benchmarks place its processing, memory bandwidth, and caching metrics within mid-tier performance percentiles, registering 11,735.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 34.66 million ops/sec in Redis tests. It is designed for compute-bound tasks, CI/CD build environments, batch processing, and high-throughput web serving.
